G7b_transfer_field_convergence.note: || G_fine - G_core ||_2 / || G_fine ||_2 on the registered 224-dimensional global class, with G the quadrature-weighted information matrix accumulated over every valid ray of each profile. This is the quantity the inverse problem consumes and the only one that depends on dx: AART's per-ray fields are analytic and carry no discretisation error. The coarse-to-core step is 4.408e-02, so refinement is reducing the change.

G7b_fields_are_analytic_not_discretised.note: AART's landing coordinates agree with the grid-free analytic kgeo to 2.6e-15 (n=0), 1.1e-13 (n=1) and 2.2e-12 (n=2), identically at the core and fine profiles. The per-ray transfer fields therefore carry no resolution dependence, which is why field-value comparison between profiles measures band steepness rather than convergence. Recorded so the reasoning behind this gate's definition is auditable.

G8t_retarded_time_validation.note: largest disagreement in a PAIRWISE emission-time difference between AART and kgeo's independent analytic solution, over 25200 pairs from 225 stratified rays, 16875 of them spanning different orders. Differences are compared so that a common time origin cancels; here the measured common offset is -2.274e-13, i.e. the two codes already share an origin. Tolerance frozen at 1e-03 M, far below any temporal structure the source model resolves.

G8t_azimuth_after_rigid_offset.note: AART and kgeo place phi = 0 on different axes. The offset is 1.570796326795 rad, exactly +1 quarter turns to 1.377e-14. A rigid rotation is a convention, as a common time origin is; what is gated is the residual once one global constant is removed.

G8t_azimuth_offset_is_order_independent.note: spread of the fitted azimuth offset across orders: {'0': 1.5707963267948932, '1': 1.570796326794984, '2': 1.5707963267948537}. This is the gate that matters. A single global rotation only relabels the azimuth axis; an order-dependent or screen-dependent one would corrupt every non-axisymmetric source model, and would not be a convention.

G8t_radius_control.note: source radius on the same stratified sample, confirming the coordinate identification used to extract t and phi is correct

G10q_retired_flat_sigma_convention.note: the superseded convention (c = g^3, flat per-row sigma) measured on the same rays: worst 7.000e+00, growing as k - 1. It manufactures Fisher information out of pixel count, and since ray counts differ by orders of magnitude between lensing bands it silently reweighted the bands against each other. Preserved as the reason the convention changed, not as a live failure.
